key_results: At near-constant We, breakup changes from peripheral mist to multiple bags to leeward ligaments as M∞ rises; higher M∞ reduces flattening/sheet growth and delays breakup.
Eight tabulated cases preserve gas/liquid pair, M∞, We, Re, Oh, density ratio, and viscosity ratio separately.

mechanisms.summary: Author interpretation: compressibility/shock-related flow structure modifies deformation and instability even when We is held near 1100; Re has a complementary but minor effect.

evidence_candidates.claim: At We near 1100, breakup morphology and timing still change substantially with post-shock freestream Mach number.
The paper's Mach number is the post-shock freestream-flow Mach, whereas We uses post-shock gas density and velocity.
